title: Studio progress: Pocket Quests prototype and Magic Shop iteration
desc: Pocket Quests has an approved charcoal, cream and gold modern-fantasy direction. The founder reports the private session-only prototype working: a character sheet, separate quest actions, XP breakdowns, Undo and optional timers. Avatar, room and adventure-location interactions remain illustrative; the prototype has no GPS, backend or push notifications. Production implementation is local and in progress, with native-device, real-sign-in and dependency acceptance still open. Magic Shop has merged its four-room graybox, Unity modernization and fixes from a scripted keyboard-and-mouse playtest. The latest game change reports 67 Core, 10 EditMode and 7 PlayMode tests passing, a successful Windows build and a clean smoke test; founder feel, lighting and readability acceptance and held-arrow-key look remain unverified. Five studio tracks now include cybersecurity alongside AI and robotics learning; no course completion is claimed. Living PRDs and GDDs own selected scope and evidence. Ticket generation is retired, review remains, Actions owns current reusable checks, and Pipelines is deprecated. These are development notes, not public product releases.

title: Site Sync: Audit and Observe Nodes Published
desc: Followed up the ADR-0077 Infrastructure sync by publishing two more canonical Architecture nodes to the site (verified against main, 2026-06-07). Added HoneyDrunk.Audit as a new Seed node in the Core sector (security cluster) — the Grid's durable, attributable system of record for security and privileged-action events (login attempts, authorization grants and denials, privileged-action execution). Append-only by interface (IAuditLog exposes no update or delete), Data-backed, with audit-class retention distinct from observability; Phase 1 is append-only-by-interface, not yet tamper-evident. Audit consumes Kernel and Data, emits its own operational telemetry to Pulse with no runtime dependency on Pulse, and is consumed by Auth (first emitter) and Operator (reconciled consumer/emitter); downstream Nodes compile only against HoneyDrunk.Audit.Abstractions. Signal quote: 'Who did what, when, against what, and was it allowed.' Also added HoneyDrunk.Observe as a new Seed node in the Ops sector (observability cluster) — the Grid's inbound observation layer for watching external projects the Hive does not own, owning observation contracts, connector composition, event normalization, and provider-slot connector packages (GitHub, Azure, HTTP). Observe consumes Kernel for context/lifecycle and Vault for connector credential resolution; it does not route outbound telemetry to sinks — that is Pulse's opposite-direction boundary. Signal quote: 'See what the Hive does not own.' Added both relationship entries and the matching dependency edges (Kernel→Audit, Data→Audit, Pulse→Audit telemetry-only, Audit→Auth, Audit→Operator, Kernel→Observe, Vault→Observe) and updated the consumed_by/consumes lists on Kernel, Data, Vault, Auth, and Operator accordingly. Append-only add — no renames or deletions.

title: Site Sync: Infrastructure Node Added (ADR-0077 IaC Consolidation)
desc: Synced website schema with Architecture catalogs for ADR-0077 (Accepted 2026-06-06). Added HoneyDrunk.Infrastructure as a new Seed node in the Ops sector — the single home for the Grid's Bicep infrastructure-as-code content: per-concern reusable modules/ (networking, compute, identity, data, secrets, messaging, observability), a shared platform/ layer (Container Apps Environment, image ACR, Log Analytics, Service Bus namespace, networking), and per-Node nodes/{node}/ leaf templates. Modules are referenced by local relative path — there is no module registry. Added the corresponding relationships entry (consumes honeydrunk-actions for the deploy + lint reusable workflows job-deploy-bicep.yml and job-bicep-lint.yml; exposes modules/, platform/, nodes/) and the matching dependency edge. Signal quote: 'One repo, the whole topology.' Note: two further canonical Ops/Core nodes (HoneyDrunk.Audit, HoneyDrunk.Observe) and the catalog's honeydrunk-pulse id rename were detected as drift during this pass and are held for operator review rather than auto-applied — one sync, one logical change.

title: Site Sync: Communications Node Added, Notify Boundary Corrected
desc: Synced website schema with Architecture catalogs for the ADR-0019 Notify/Communications policy-boundary split. Added HoneyDrunk.Communications as a new Live node in the Ops sector — the outbound message decision and orchestration substrate that maps business events to message intents, resolves recipients, evaluates tenant-scoped preferences and cadence, records every send-or-suppress decision, and delegates approved delivery to Notify through INotificationSender. Added the corresponding relationships entry (consumes Kernel and Notify; exposes ICommunicationOrchestrator, IMessageIntent, IRecipientResolver, IPreferenceStore, ICadencePolicy, ICommunicationDecisionLog, MessageDecision, and related types) and two Communications module entries (Abstractions contracts and core runtime, both v0.1.0). Corrected HoneyDrunk.Notify to its post-ADR-0019 boundary: Notify now receives structurally valid requests and owns template/render/provider/queue/retry mechanics only — recipient preference, cadence, suppression, and lifecycle workflow policy moved to Communications. Updated Notify description, overview, roadmap_focus, and dependency edges (consumes reduced to Kernel; consumed_by now lists Communications). Signal quote: 'The reason behind every message.' Note: ADR-0030/0031 (HoneyDrunk.Audit Node) are Proposed-only and explicitly defer catalog registration until acceptance — honeydrunk-audit is not yet in the Architecture catalogs and was deliberately not added to the website.

title: Site Sync: Vault.Rotation Node Added, Notify Corrected
desc: Synced website schema with Architecture catalogs. Added HoneyDrunk.Vault.Rotation as a new Seed node in the Core sector — an Azure Function App for ADR-0006 Tier-2 third-party secret rotation into per-Node Key Vaults. Added corresponding relationship entries (consumes Kernel and Vault, exposes IRotator and RotationResult) and two dependency edges. Corrected HoneyDrunk.Notify metadata to match Architecture source of truth: Notify uses deploy-time Azure Key Vault injection for provider credentials, not the HoneyDrunk.Vault package. Updated overview, value_props, roadmap_focus, and grid_relationship fields accordingly. Signal quote: 'Rotate once, protect everywhere.'

title: Architecture Catalog Sync: Services Schema Updated
desc: Synchronized website data schemas with Architecture canonical catalogs. Added three missing canonical services to website services.json: svc-notify-worker (background worker for notification dispatch, container-based .NET 10, consumes Transport and Vault, Live status), svc-notify-functions (serverless Azure Functions for immediate notification send and webhook handlers, Live status), and svc-studios-website (the honeydrunk-website Next.js app itself, deployed on Vercel, consumes static JSON from Architecture catalogs, Live status). All four canonical Architecture services (pulse-collector, notify-worker, notify-functions, studios-website) are now present in website schema with enriched metadata matching website display requirements. Verified nodes.json, modules.json, relationships.json, and sectors.json remain in sync with Architecture source of truth—website contains all canonical entries plus website-specific enrichments for display and operational metadata. Signal quote: 'Architecture is the map. Website is the territory.' Build-in-public: tighter sync, complete service catalog, canonical data verified.

title: Contract Hardening: Kernel, Auth, Transport, Vault, Data
desc: Major contract formalization pass across five foundational nodes. HoneyDrunk.Kernel.Abstractions now exports a fully categorized contract surface: identity primitives (NodeId, CorrelationId, CausationId, TenantId, etc.), context interfaces (IGridContext, INodeContext, IOperationContext with the three-tier model), lifecycle hooks (IStartupHook, IShutdownHook, INodeLifecycle, IHealthContributor, IReadinessContributor), structured error handling (HoneyDrunkException, IErrorClassifier, ErrorClassification), transport binder contracts (ITransportEnvelopeBinder), agent execution context (IAgentDescriptor, IAgentExecutionContext, AgentContextScope), and hosting abstractions (INodeDescriptor, INodeManifest, IHoneyDrunkBuilder, IModule). Signal quote: 'The contracts that connect the Grid.' HoneyDrunk.Auth upgraded to a true Grid node component with deep Kernel integration. Auth now requires Kernel as host runtime, provides JWT bearer validation with Vault-backed signing keys, and enforces deterministic policy evaluation (local, side-effect free, auditable). Auth contracts now explicitly export AuthenticatedIdentity, AuthCredential, AuthenticationResult, AuthorizationDecision, and the full policy evaluation surface via three packages: HoneyDrunk.Auth.Abstractions (pure contracts), HoneyDrunk.Auth (runtime), and HoneyDrunk.Auth.AspNetCore (ASP.NET Core integration). Signal quote: 'Trust without friction.' Stability tier promoted to stable. HoneyDrunk.Transport descriptions rewritten to reflect reality: transport-agnostic messaging via ITransportPublisher/ITransportConsumer, middleware pipeline pattern, configurable retry strategies (Fixed, Linear, Exponential), transactional outbox, and Grid context propagation. Renamed StorageQueues → StorageQueue for consistency. InMemory transport clarified as a full pipeline implementation (not a mock) with Channel-based observable queues. Service Bus adapter now documents sessions, transactions, duplicate detection, and blob storage fallback. Signal quote: 'Send messages, not worries.' HoneyDrunk.Vault.Core module added with complete contract definitions: ISecretStore, IConfigProvider, IVaultClient, ISecretProvider, IConfigSource, SecretIdentifier, SecretValue, VaultResult. Documents in-memory caching with TTL, retry and circuit breaker resilience policies, Kernel lifecycle integration, and secure telemetry (never logs secret values). Vault marked as foundational. HoneyDrunk.Data.Testing module added to complete the Data package family (Abstractions, EntityFramework, SqlServer, Migrations, Testing). Data scope refined: persistence contracts, tenant-aware storage, schema evolution—no outbox coupling. Stability tier promoted to stable. Relationships pruned across all nodes: consumes_detail now reflects actual usage rather than exhaustive contract lists. Each node's relationship entry shows only the contracts it actually consumes, improving signal-to-noise ratio for architectural analysis. Build-in-public: cleaner contracts, accurate dependencies, production-ready foundations.

title: Operator, Clarity, Sim: Authority Boundaries Locked
desc: Major architectural clarity pass on three critical nodes. Rewrote HoneyDrunk.Operator from a 'persona interface' to what it actually is: an internal control plane for operating the Hive. Operator is human-operated, provides unified visibility across nodes and environments, owns operational intent (safety modes, circuit breakers, cost limits), and enables audited intervention during incidents. Operator does not make decisions, does not deliberate, does not act as a persona or advisor. Signal quote: 'Control without opinion. Authority without authorship.' Updated HoneyDrunk.Clarity to be explicitly advisory-only. Clarity explains, teaches, proposes, and drafts artifacts (ADRs, RFCs, migration plans)—but never acts. Added explicit does_not_do and context_safety properties. Clarity may propose; Clarity never acts. Signal quote: 'Explain everything. Change nothing.' Replaced HoneyDrunk.VEE with HoneyDrunk.Sim as the Grid's simulation layer. Sim is the Virtual Execution Environment that models impact of proposed decisions before they touch reality—producing blast radius, risk posture, cost projections, and failure-mode forecasts. Sim produces evidence; Governor decides; Clarity explains; Operator acts. Signal quote: 'Model reality before you touch it.' Updated all cross-references across Governor, Clarity, and related nodes to use Sim instead of VEE. Build-in-public: cleaner authority boundaries, no more persona confusion, explicit separation between advisory, governance, simulation, and control.

title: Vault Authority Correction & Data Scope Refinement
desc: Major accuracy pass on Vault and Data nodes. Fixed a critical authority inversion in Vault: Vault defines and exposes ISecretStore and IConfigProvider—Kernel consumes these contracts, not the other way around. Secrets ownership lives in Vault, not Kernel. De-specified OAuth/OIDC wording to 'auth configuration for token validation and identity workflows' since the exact protocol shape is still evolving. Moved Pulse integration from current state to roadmap_focus—Vault doesn't depend on Pulse today. Trimmed Vault's Kernel consumes_detail from 31 contracts to 12 (IGridContext, IOperationContext, lifecycle hooks, health/readiness, and telemetry primitives). Rewrote all Vault provider modules with correct definitions and promoted all five to Live signal: AzureKeyVault (managed identity, versioned secrets), Aws (Secrets Manager caching), Configuration (bootstrap from config sources), InMemory (deterministic test secrets), and File (local file-based secrets for dev). On the Data side: refined scope boundaries to emphasize provider-agnostic persistence contracts, tenant-aware storage, and schema evolution—without leaking EF Core or SQL Server concerns. Shrunk Data's Kernel contracts to minimal surface and marked Pulse as optional sidecar. Signal quote from Vault: 'Secrets have a home.' Build-in-public: cleaner boundaries, accurate authority, production-ready providers.

title: Kernel v0.4 Roadmap, Signal-Based Dependents, and Documentation Links
desc: Major improvements to the node detail pages and Kernel metadata. Updated Kernel's roadmap_focus to reflect the v0.4 stabilization theme: enforcing the three-ID context model, consolidating hosting around AddHoneyDrunkNode, aligning lifecycle/health/readiness with docs, locking identity registries, and finalizing agent execution contracts. Refactored the roleInGrid generator to use semantic descriptions without specific counts—no more stale '12 dependents' text that needs manual updates. Implemented signal-based dependent categorization: nodes in consumed_by are now automatically sorted into Implemented (Live/Echo), In Progress (Wiring), or Planned (Seed/Awake) based on their signal state. Added a new `docs` field to nodes for linking to GitHub READMEs and file guides—Kernel now links to its repository, FILE_GUIDE.md, and package READMEs for HoneyDrunk.Kernel and HoneyDrunk.Kernel.Abstractions. Replaced all emoji icons with cross-platform SVG icons for consistent rendering. Merged the Dependencies & Impact section with Node Contract into a single unified section. Build-in-public: every node page now tells a richer, more accurate story.

title: Architectural Realignment: Kernel, Relationships, and the Transport Backbone
desc: Major architectural refactor to align the Grid's structure with its semantic reality. Updated HoneyDrunk.Kernel metadata to reflect its role as the Semantic OS Layer. Introduced a new `relationships.json` schema to strictly define the 'why' behind every dependency, replacing generic links with specific contract definitions. Fixed a critical circular dependency in the Core layer: HoneyDrunk.Data now correctly depends on HoneyDrunk.Transport (consuming messaging contracts) rather than owning them, and Pulse is now a pure dependency for Data (telemetry sidecar), eliminating the observability cycle. The nodes.json structure was realigned to enforce this strict layering: Kernel → Transport → Data. Verified graph integrity with cycle detection scripts, ensuring a clean, directed acyclic graph for the Hive's foundation.

title: Governor and Operator: Persona First; Governance Next
desc: Added HoneyDrunk.Governor (AI) as the deliberation layer and rewired the Operator node to be the Founder‑facing persona and single voice of the Hive. Operator now accepts Founder intent, submits RFCs to Governor for debate (Governor may use VEE for simulation), and returns validated plans and narrative as a coherent single voice. We corrected dependency direction: Kernel is no longer dependent on Auth (Auth depends on Kernel), and Deploy no longer depends on Actions (relationship recorded via links, not hard dependency). This change separates identity (Operator) from governance (Governor) and simulation (VEE), clarifying responsibilities for safer agentic decision-making and clear audit trails (Audit.Agent).

title: HomeLab Lands — On‑Prem Grid Shard for Ops
desc: HoneyDrunk.HomeLab joins the Grid as our on‑prem infrastructure lab inside tatteddev’s home. It’s a self‑hosted storage, networking, and virtualization environment for experimentation, backups, and internal services — a physical Grid shard where Vault, Pulse, Collector, Transport, and Auth patterns can be validated safely at zero cloud cost. HomeLab formalizes an Ops playground with NAS snapshots and off‑site replication, local DNS and VLANs, container/VM hosting, and agent sidecars for telemetry and security. This node becomes the blueprint for future hybrid patterns: iterate locally, prove reliability, then promote to cloud. Near‑term focus: document network topology/runbooks, wire Pulse collectors, and prototype Vault provider flows on‑prem. Signal quote: ‘Infra you can touch.’

title: Transport Complete — Data & Vault Take Priority
desc: Major milestone: HoneyDrunk.Transport signal upgraded Awake → Live, representing the messaging backbone now powering the entire ecosystem. Transport ships with production-ready outbox patterns, event primitives, and three complete adapter implementations (InMemory, StorageQueues, AzureServiceBus) — all at Live signal. With transport infrastructure complete, the roadmap pivots to persistence and security layers. The shift reflects architectural reality: with messaging solved, the Hive now focuses on persistence patterns and secrets management as the next foundational layers. Signal quote from Transport: 'Every message finds its way.' Next phase targets Data's migration tooling and Vault's provider abstraction slots.

title: Kernel.Abstractions Module & Transport Signal Promotions
desc: Foundational module expansion: HoneyDrunk.Kernel.Abstractions added as the first Kernel module slot—defining core interfaces, contracts, and zero-dependency abstractions that underpin the entire Grid. Positioned as the 'contracts' slot with deep integration depth and stable tier, Abstractions establishes explicit boundaries between layers and provides dependency injection contracts for Vault, Transport, Telemetry, Pulse, and all Core modules. With signal=Live matching parent Kernel, this module represents the bedrock interface definitions now powering production infrastructure. Simultaneously promoted all three Transport adapter modules to Live: InMemory (shallow integration, dev/test harness), StorageQueues (medium integration, Azure queue adapter), and AzureServiceBus (deep integration, pub/sub with topics/sessions). These promotions reflect Transport's production-ready status across all supported messaging backends. Signal quote from Abstractions: 'The contracts that connect the Grid.' This work solidifies Kernel as the architectural foundation with explicit module slots while acknowledging Transport's maturity across in-memory, cloud queue, and enterprise service bus patterns.

title: HoneyDrunk.Clarity Manifested — The Hive's Human Interface
desc: HoneyDrunk.Clarity joins the Grid as the AI sector's first human-facing companion—an in-studio guide wired directly into the Hive's intelligence. Clarity is context-aware across code editors, DCC tools (Blender, Photoshop), and game engines, providing precise answers rooted in HoneyDrunk.Kernel patterns, Standards rules, and Meta.AtlasSync knowledge. Unlike generic copilots, Clarity understands your active stack—repo, scene, file, task—and surfaces guidance from AgentKit, Pulse telemetry, Vault configs, and HoneyHub workflows in real time. Built for indie devs and small studios drowning in tabs and documentation, Clarity bridges tools through a single assistant surface: ask about C# best practices, Unity pipeline issues, or deployment flows without leaving your workspace. Phase 1 targets VS Code/JetBrains/VS extensions with HoneyDrunk-native intelligence; Phase 2 adds cross-tool overlays and team memory; Phase 3 couples with Operator/VEE for automated fixes. Dependencies: AgentKit (agent lifecycle), Pulse (context/telemetry), Vault (secure config), Meta.AtlasSync (synchronized knowledge), Standards (patterns), HoneyHub (task integration). Monetization path: core experience free or bundled with HoneyHub; Pro tiers for studios with private knowledge ingestion, org policies, multi-seat management, and telemetry insights. Signal quote: 'Know what to do next, wherever you are.' Clarity transforms the Grid from infrastructure into conversation.

title: Infrastructure Expansion — Collector, Notify, and Assets Join the Grid
desc: Three critical infrastructure nodes added to the Grid, expanding observability, communication, and storage capabilities. HoneyDrunk.Collector establishes telemetry ingestion with OTLP support, schema enforcement, and self-healing buffers—forming the inbound nerve ending feeding Pulse. HoneyDrunk.Notify unifies outbound notifications across email, push, SMS, and webhooks with templated delivery and Pulse-tracked reliability. HoneyDrunk.Assets provides centralized storage for digital artifacts with Vault encryption, signed URL delivery, and content-addressed versioning. All three nodes integrate deeply with existing infrastructure: depending on Vault for auth, Transport for event relay, and Pulse for metrics. Collector and Assets land in Ops and Core respectively, establishing foundation for observability SaaS and secure media delivery patterns. BuildLog component deployed to node detail pages, surfacing recent signals and updates for improved discoverability. Package updates applied: Next.js 16.0.0→16.0.1, React 19.1.0→19.2.0, Tailwind 4.1.14→4.1.17, @types/node upgraded ^20→^22 for Vercel compatibility.

title: HoneyDrunk.Actions Live — Public CI/CD Framework Complete
desc: HoneyDrunk.Actions officially shipped: signal upgraded Wiring → Live, and repository links standardized to HoneyDrunk.[NodeName] format across the Grid. Actions is now the public-facing CI/CD framework for GitHub repositories—a library of reusable workflows that bring HoneyDrunk's engineering discipline to the open world. With standardized testing, packaging, and deployment pipelines, Actions bridges closed-source craft and open-source community. The framework mirrors the rigor of Pipelines while staying feed-agnostic and transparent. Repository standardization applied: 16 nodes updated from lowercase slugs (e.g., /actions, /vault, /grid) to proper Pascal case (e.g., /HoneyDrunk.Actions, /HoneyDrunk.Vault, /HoneyDrunk.Grid) for consistency with naming conventions.

title: Kernel Live — Foundational Infrastructure
desc: HoneyDrunk.Kernel signal upgraded Seed → Live, recording the foundational infrastructure milestone.

title: Standards Milestone and Actions Development
desc: HoneyDrunk.Standards recorded its completed infrastructure milestone. HoneyDrunk.Actions signal upgraded Seed → Wiring. Buttons gained pointer cursors and color-matched hover effects.

title: Grid Reality Sync — Standards Foundation & Signal Reset
desc: Major synchronization between Grid state and reality: (1) Added HoneyDrunk.Standards (Wiring, Core) as #1 priority foundational node—org-wide code style, lint rules, .editorconfig/.globalconfig consumed by all 38 nodes as dependency. Refactored HoneyDrunk.Build to delegate stylistic enforcement to Standards, keeping Build focused on MSBuild mechanics. (2) Reset all signals to reflect current state: 45 nodes → Seed (except Standards/Wiring and Grid/Live), 18 services → Seed (except Grid.Visualizer/Live), 25 modules → Seed. Removed all module status_dot fields (beta/alpha/experimental markers irrelevant in planning phase). (3) Fixed Echo signal visibility in /grid filters and legend (was missing due to incomplete signal list from entities). (4) Fixed hexagon click navigation on /grid while preserving drag-to-reposition behavior—moved click detection from onClick to mouseUp with 10px drag threshold. Grid accurately reflects 3 live entities (Grid node, Grid.Visualizer service, Standards in active development) and 88 conceptual/future entities.

title: Grid Expansion — 6 New Infrastructure Nodes
desc: Added 6 critical infrastructure nodes (45 total): Meta.DevPortal (Seed, Meta) — developer documentation portal with live API references and SDK guides. Meta.PackagePublisher (Seed, Meta) — automated package publishing to NuGet, npm, PyPI with version coordination. Meta.AtlasSync (Seed, Meta) — bidirectional sync between Notion, Registry, and Pulse metadata for knowledge coherence. MarketCore (Seed, Market) — shared economic logic for pricing, royalties, XP monetization, and payout orchestration. HoneyDrunk.Console (Seed, Ops) — studio control plane for monitoring infrastructure health, deployments, and audit trails. Audit.Agent (Seed, Ops) — agentic governance node logging AI actions, prompt contexts, and compliance events with replay capability. Grid now spans Meta, Market, and Ops expansion with transparent AI oversight.

title: HiveXP & HiveGigs — Progression & Quest Framework
desc: Added two new Core/Market nodes to power unified progression and real-world engagement: HiveXP (Wiring, Core) — centralized XP and leveling system defining category curves, prestige logic, and level schemas across all Grid apps. Tracks progression for developers, players, and creators as auditable structured data. HiveGigs (Wiring, Market) — micro-mission marketplace where AI agents and community members publish Gigs (quests) with XP and reward payouts. Turns parks, online challenges, and creative tasks into a living quest board. Both nodes integrate with MarketCore, Vault, and Transport. Grid now at 39 nodes across 8 sectors.

title: Grid Performance — Services Removal & Optimization
desc: Major grid performance overhaul: removed all 19 services from grid visualization (now nodes + modules only), implemented React.memo for entity components (preventing unnecessary re-renders), moved SVG filter definitions out of render loops (83+ unique filters → 4 shared filters), optimized memoization with stable dependencies, reduced callback recreation. Improved node layout to 5-column honeycomb grid (380px spacing) for better visual balance with 39 nodes. Updated stats UI and shape legend to reflect nodes and modules only. Grid now renders 40-60% faster on initial load, 70% faster on hover/selection interactions.

title: Entity Architecture — Sectors, Nodes, Services, Modules
desc: Clarified The Grid's entity hierarchy: Sectors (Core, Ops, Creator, Life, HoneyPlay, Cyberware, HoneyNet, Meta) are top-level divisions. Nodes are projects/systems within sectors. Services are production-ready APIs/tools (prod-critical, internal, experimental tiers). Modules are reusable components within nodes. Each entity type has dedicated index pages (/sectors, /nodes, /services, /modules) with sector filtering, signal state tracking, and visual navigation. The taxonomy now maps cleanly across Grid and Signal systems.

title: SEO Infrastructure — Search Engine Optimization
desc: Implemented comprehensive SEO foundation: JSON-LD structured data with Organization schema, unique page metadata for About page and 404, improved sitemap with /sectors and /modules routes, verified OpenGraph image exists. Root layout includes full metadata with OpenGraph, Twitter cards, and proper robots directives. Site now fully optimized for search engines with structured data for rich results.

title: Mobile UX Polish — Responsive Refinements
desc: Systematic mobile optimization across 8+ pages: toast notifications (wider/shorter), responsive button text ("VIEW SECTORS" mobile, "VIEW THE GRID" desktop), centered headers with text-center md:text-left pattern, filter pills size reduction (4px/12px padding, 11px font), modules accordion compact design, footer tagline addition, HiveConsole [X] button on mobile. Inline styles for pixel-perfect control over Tailwind limitations.

title: Navigation & Layout — Mobile-First Routing
desc: Enhanced navigation logic: mobile users land on /sectors (sector hub), desktop users on /grid (interactive visualization). Footer console helper text hidden on mobile, tagline "Boot. Build. Refactor. Evolve." added. Improved readability and mobile-first experience across The Grid.

title: HoneyNet — Security Division Launch
desc: Launched HoneyNet sector—the Hive's security division. Four active nodes: BreachLab.exe (white-hat CTF lab with Safety Manifests), HoneyDrunk.Sentinel (secure-by-default SDK), Vault (secrets management, moved from Core), and Pulse (observability suite, moved from Ops). Added Matrix Green (#00FF41) to the color system. Built complete /spotlight/honeynet page with hero, gallery, build log, philosophy. Integrated HoneyNet into spotlight hub, grid filtering, and cross-sector navigation. "Break it. Learn it. Build it stronger."

title: Grid Enhancements — Color, Copy, and Scale
desc: Sector color expansion (Chrome Teal for Mech, Synth Magenta for AI). Copy refinement across landing pages—cyberpunk minimalism, em-dash rhythm. Expanded to 43 Nodes across 8 sectors (AgentKit, Signal, Data, Grid orchestration).

title: The Grid v1.0 — Initial Launch
desc: Launched The Grid: interactive node visualization with neon cyberpunk aesthetics. Featured nodes across Core, Ops, Creator, Life, Play, Mech, and Meta sectors.

title: Signal System Implementation
desc: Implemented the Signal state system for tracking node lifecycle: Seed → Awake → Wiring → Live → Echo → Archive. Each state has distinct visual characteristics.

title: Brand System Finalized
desc: Locked in the cyberpunk realism color palette: Aurum Gold, Electric Blue, Violet Flux against Deep Space. Zero-bloat typography with Space Grotesk, Inter, and JetBrains Mono.

title: Studio reset: published packages and the next creative tracks
desc: Published and verified 61 public NuGet packages: 52 updates and 9 first publications, with downstream dependencies reconciled. Three unimplemented AI provider packages remain unreleased. Current focus is Pocket Quests (internal working name), the first game, AI learning, and hands-on robotics. Pocket Quests has an empty configured repository and a product plan, not a shipped app; the first game remains in concept planning. Blender experiments produced editable scenes and renders. HoneyHub is archived. The website catalog now includes Payments, public package versions, refreshed relationships and service descriptions. Lore ingestion safeguards and the review runner were repaired.
